svg.aria-label: Animated credit card payment lifecycle: OCR, authorization, clearing and settlement
svg.text: Interactive architecture from Card Capture to Settlement

g.text: The cardholder presents their credit card physically at a POS terminal or inputs
details into an online e-commerce checkout form.
The camera/scanner captures the card image, employing advanced OCR algorithms to
extract Primary Account Number (PAN), expiry date, and cardholder name instantly.
Extracted sensitive card data is immediately encrypted using TLS and tokenized by the
payment SDK to protect primary account numbers from interception.
The Payment Gateway receives the encrypted payload, performs fraud screening (e.g., 3D
Secure, Velocity checks), and routes the transaction to the merchant's Acquirer Bank.
The Acquirer Bank formats the transaction into an ISO 8583 Message Type Identifier
(MTI) 0100 Authorization Request and forwards it to the Card Scheme Network.
The Card Scheme (Visa/Mastercard) acts as the central switch, routing the ISO 8583
authorization message securely to the correct Cardholder's Issuing Bank.
The Issuing Bank receives the request, verifies account balance, performs anti-fraud
evaluation, validates CVV/AVS, and approves or declines the transaction.
The approval response flows back through Card Scheme -> Acquirer Bank -> Payment
Gateway -> Merchant POS, confirming funds are authorized and held.
At end-of-day, the Acquirer Bank aggregates all approved transactions into a batch
file and submits a Clearing Request (MTI 1200) to the Card Scheme.
The Card Scheme reconciles debits and credits between the Acquirer and Issuing banks,
calculating interchange fees and net settlement positions.
Funds are transferred from the Issuing Bank to the Acquirer Bank via central bank
settlement accounts, completing the full payment lifecycle.
